summary: Feed s091_single is degraded: IDS port (1 Gbps) is severely overloaded by 4.04 Gbps microbursts (404% of capacity). All other visibility checks (duplicates, encryption, VLAN, one-way, drops) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding the full aggregated traffic out a single 1 Gbps IDS port with no load-balancing, filtering, or burst mitigation. 1ms microbursts peak at 4.04 Gbps, exceeding port buffers and the 80% (0.8 Gbps) safe threshold across 2 intervals.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS NIC and capture buffers drop packets randomly under overload. With needs_full_payload=true and needs_both_directions=true, drops cause missed signatures, broken flow reassembly, and blind spots for detection, sharply reducing IDS coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute 4+ Gbps bursts across 4-5 IDS ports/instances via bidirectional 5-tuple hashing so each port stays below 80% utilization, preserving full payload and both directions for stateful IDS inspection without drops. Alternative is filtered feed or higher-speed port if scaling IDS is not possible.
